source: decompiled with ilspycmd from the QA profile interop assemblies; every member below is an interop wrapper around an IL2CPP method, so presence and signature are evidence and a method body is not

members.name: TriggerReload
members.role: the reload entry point this row calls on the holder's machine

members.name: CanReloadCurrent
members.role: the game's own refusal, read before the write so an impossible reload is refused rather than counted

members.name: DoReload
members.role: the body TriggerReload reaches; not called directly, recorded so the call edge is known

members.name: WieldedItem
members.role: the item the request must be about: the reload body reads the wielded item, so a request for anything else is refused by this package

members2.name: TriggerReload
members2.role: the local override; the machine that holds the weapon is the machine whose local inventory runs it

members.name: SetCurrentClip
members.role: the clip write this row calls; the game's own reload and pickup paths use the same setter

members.name: GetCurrentClip
members.role: the read-back the result row reports

members.name: GetMaxClip
members.role: the capacity a `set` request is refused against and a `fill` request is resolved to

members.name: m_clip
members.role: the field behind the accessors; not written directly, recorded because it shows the clip is per weapon instance

unverified: Whether SetCurrentClip replicates to the other machines on its own. If it does not, the host sees a stale clip until the next native sync; this is a game-verification point, not a code decision.

members.name: UpdateFireMaster
members.role: the master's own firing update; the ammunition delta around it is one shot

members.name: UpdateFireClient
members.role: the client copy; deliberately not hooked, because the ammunition this fact reads moves on the master

members.name: m_core
members.role: the device the component fires for; the placement table keys on it

members.name: OnBulletFired
members.role: the per-shot presentation callback; deliberately not used as the fact source because it is assigned by the instance and is not the ammunition

members2.name: Ammo
members2.role: the ammunition before and after the firing update

members2.name: AmmoMaxCap
members2.role: recorded, not published: the depletion fact is the zero the game reached, not a ratio

members.name: FireBurst
members.role: one glue launch (a burst of projectiles)

members.name: FireSingle
members.role: the other launch body; both are hooked and deduped per frame

unverified: Whether the glue gun's launch happens on the holder's machine only. The fact is published where the body runs, so a machine that never runs it publishes nothing rather than a duplicate.

members.name: TriggerDetonate
members.role: the mine's own trigger; `DoExplode` is reached from it, so hooking the trigger publishes once per detonation rather than once per damage application

members.name: m_core
members.role: the device instance behind the trigger component, resolved through the placement table

kernel_entry_points: RuntimeKernel.EnterOwner (host half: resolve the holder session and record the intent)
RuntimeKernel.ExecuteOwnerCommand (holder half: invoke the same handler with IsHost false, keep the result and publish its facts)
channel.wire: the existing CommandRequest message with NodeIndex = NetworkProtocol.OwnerNodeIndex (2); the endpoint slot carries the holder's session and the payload the host's resolved inputs
channel.session_resolution: RuntimeModule.OwnerSessions, keyed by capability id; ForgeWeapon answers from the placed instance's own owner chain (item -> agent -> SNet_Player -> Lookup). An equipment life is told apart from another machine by the local-player check in IsLocalHolder, which compares the local session against the agent's own player slot.
unverified: That a client's SNet_Player.Lookup is the session id the host's endpoint slot must name. It is this package's reading of the session layer, and the presentation tier's recipient list uses the same ids, so a mismatch would show up there first.
That SNet.HasLocalPlayer/PlayerAgent is populated on a dedicated server host that has no local player; the resolver answers null there and the tier refuses the step.
